transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-08-21, 15:00 - 15:58 PT | Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Auriga Head of Security), Marta Rivera (Procurement), Noah Kim (Cloud Infra), Sana Patel (Legal), Evelyn Cho (Risk)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run through the SIG/q walk. i'm jordan, AE on redwood, priya's with me for the technical bits.
[00:08] Liam: yep thanks, quick context, auriga is evaluating vendors for customer-facing chat assistant and some internal summarization — primary concern is evidence for SOC 2, encryption, and data residency.
[00:20] Priya: great, we'll go question by question, i'll note where we need to attach artifacts. i'll also call out differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
[00:29] Marta: procurement needs timeline — we have an RFP window, would like vendor evidence within a week if possible.
[00:35] Jordan: understood, we'll aim to return the completed SIG and links by monday, that's what we're aiming for.
[00:42] Priya: starting Q1 — organizational security, do you have SOC 2? we've got a SOC 2 Type II attestation, current through 2026-06, i'll attach the pdf.
[00:52] Sana: is there an ISO 27001 cert as well?
[00:55] Priya: we don't have ISO cert at this time, we do have mapped controls and an ISO readiness gap plan, i can share the gap report.
[01:05] Noah: for SOC 2, do you support customer-specific logs / audit exports? auriga needs audit trails shipped to our SIEM.
[01:12] Priya: yes — Redwood Console exposes audit logs, and for Private we can stream logs to a customer-managed syslog or S3 bucket. Hosted API has export options and can push to our logging pipeline — we'll share doc and sample log schema.
[01:23] [01:23] Liam: ok can you clarify retention and who controls retention?
[01:27] Priya: retention depends on deployment: Hosted retains default for X days (we'll include exact), Dedicated can have configurable retention per contract, Private the customer controls retention in their environment. we'll provide the retention matrix.
[01:40] Jordan: next, encryption at rest and key mgmt. question in SIG asks if customer keys are supported.
[01:46] Priya: we support CMEK for Dedicated and Private; you can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or HSM via standard APIs. Hosted support for CMEK is possible under enterprise contracts — we'll call that out.
[01:58] Marta: for regulatory, we need HSM-backed key storage for production keys. is that supported?
[02:03] Priya: yes, HSM-backed KMS integration is supported on Private — we'll include an architecture diagram showing the key flow and where keys are held.
[02:11] Jordan: CAIQ crosswalk question — data residency and geo restrictions.
[02:15] Priya: Redwood Dedicated provides region pinning; Private lets you run in-app in your VPC or on-prem. for hosted API, we operate in specific cloud regions and can sign data residency commitments in enterprise agreements. we'll include region list and data residency attestation.
[02:30] Evelyn: do you do in-transit encryption for internal service-to-service traffic?
[02:34] Priya: yes, mutual TLS between services for Dedicated/Private, and TLS1.2+ for hosted endpoints. we'll include cipher suites list.
[02:44] Liam: about RBAC and SSO — integration with our SAML provider?
[02:48] Priya: Redwood Console supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC is role-based roles for admins, viewers, billing, etc. for Dedicated/Private you can map to your IdP groups.
[02:59] Noah: do you support attribute-based access control / custom roles?
[03:03] Priya: we have custom roles in the roadmap, today we support predefined roles and granular permissions per route/model. i'll share the RBAC matrix.
[03:12] Marta: procurement question — will you provide answers directly in our vendor portal (Coupa-like) or do we need to upload a PDF?
[03:18] Jordan: we can upload to your portal or provide the raw SIG/CAIQ files plus evidence links. whichever you prefer.
[03:24] [03:24] Sana: legal wants to confirm data processing addendum (DPA) and that redwood will sign for data processor responsibilities.
[03:29] Jordan: yes we have a standard DPA, and enterprise DPA adjustments are possible. we'll attach the DPA and sample contract clauses.
[03:36] Priya: moving to technical deep dive items on the SIG — question about model artifacts and customer data exposure. we do not persist customer inputs in long-term model training for hosted without explicit opt-in; there's an opt-in flag for training. Dedicated/Private never share data outside customer tenancy.
[03:53] Liam: can we get a statement to that effect for procurement?
[03:56] Jordan: yes, we'll include the training data policy statement.
[04:01] Noah: for the pilot we plan to use Dedicated; what are the network requirements?
[04:06] Priya: for Dedicated we'll provide IP ranges and egress/ingress rules. for Private we'll need peering/VPN or direct connect and firewall ports — i'll attach a runbook with sample iptables and exact ports.
[04:18] [04:18] Liam: evidence requests: SOC 2 attestation, penetration test summary, architecture diagram, KMS integration doc, RBAC docs, SSO config guide, sample audit logs — anything else?
[04:28] Priya: also include our incident response policy, vulnerability disclosure program and third-party vendor assessments.
[04:34] Marta: timeline again — can you get all artifacts in a week?
[04:38] Jordan: yes, we're targeting 2026-08-24 for the first bundle; Priya will follow up with tech docs.
[04:45] Sana: legal will review the SOC 2 and DPA, might have redlines.
[04:49] Priya: a few SIG-specific clarifications: question on crypto key lifecycle — we will provide key rotation cadence for CMEK, and HSM usage details. note that some transcript text may have mis-heard acronyms — CAIQ vs CAIQx, but we'll use the official CAIQ template.
[05:05] Jordan: we also get the question about endpoint-level signing of requests for non-repudiation?
[05:09] Priya: we can support signed webhooks and request signing for critical flows — we'll include the webhook signing spec.
[05:16] [05:16] Liam: ok, internal reviewers will want to see redwood's change management / release notes cadence and whether you do canary deploys.
[05:23] Priya: yes, we do canary rollouts, per-route model pins, and we can enable automatic fallback to smaller models in capacity events. we'll attach the deployment policies doc.
[05:35] Noah: for audit logs — can you forward logs to our Splunk / Azure Sentinel, how is identity mapped?
[05:40] Priya: we support streaming JSON logs to S3 or syslog, and can integrate with Splunk HTTP Event Collector. identity mapping will include requesting user, API key, model, and route.
[05:49] Marta: will you redact PII in logs?
[05:52] Priya: by default logs contain request metadata; payload redaction is configurable in Private/Dedicated; for Hosted we can apply redaction policies per agreement. we'll provide options.
[06:02] Jordan: last one — pen test frequency and results?
[06:06] Priya: annual third-party penetration test and quarterly internal scans; we'll provide the executive summary and remediation tracker. full reports are under NDA, we can provide to security teams.
[06:16] [06:16] Sana: sounds good, legal will follow up re: NDA for full pentest docs.
[06:20] Jordan: recap and next steps: we'll upload SIG answers, attach SOC 2 pdf, architecture diagrams, RBAC/SSO guides, KMS integration doc, log examples, and schedule an infra session.
[06:30] Liam: thanks, we'll look for the bundle and then coordinate with procurement.
[06:35] Jordan: thanks all, end of call.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few errors (e.g., Redwood Dedicate -> Redwood Dedicated, CAIQ variations). We included names and timestamps but some speaker labels may be approximate.
